data.licence: No third-party data in this run: the input CSVs are generated by synthetic_afsis.py in this repository. The real AfSIS Phase I set (downloaded from s3://afsis, AWS Open Data) is licensed ODbL / ODC-By; that licence is NOT inherited by these numbers.

synthetic_specification.true_model: SOC = (1.90 + 0.55*a_r) + (0.22 + 0.18*b_r)*(clay-28)/10 - 0.55*(EC-0.2) - 0.15*(pH-6.0) + N(0,0.35); a_r and b_r are per-REGION draws and each region is a compact geographic cluster, so the relationship is non-stationary in space. clay also shifts with a_r, which lets a random split partly recognise a region from its features.
synthetic_specification.designed_to_show: a gap between random CV and spatially blocked CV. This is a property of the simulation, chosen so the pipeline can be tested; it is NOT a claim about African soils.
synthetic_specification.warning: SYNTHETIC: numbers from this dataset describe a simulation, not African soils. Do not cite.

validation.spatial_grouping: KMeans on per-site coordinate centroids -> GroupKFold; records of one site/profile always share a fold
validation.tuning: GridSearchCV inside every training fold (nested CV); imputation and scaling fitted on training folds only
validation.spatial_partition_note: The main comparison builds the spatial partition ONCE (KMeans seeded with --seed0) and reuses it for every model, seed and scheme, so random-vs-spatial is a paired comparison. The SD across seeds of a spatial-CV cell therefore measures learner randomness only and is exactly 0.000 for deterministic models (ridge, PLS). The uncertainty of where the block boundaries fall is reported separately in results.partition_sensitivity and results.block_sensitivity, not hidden inside the 0.000.

experiment_scope.note: Parallelism affects wall-clock only: every grid candidate is a separate seeded fit, so R2 is identical at n_jobs=1 and n_jobs=4 (checked). --quick additionally skips nested tuning; it is for tests, never for reported numbers.

partition_sensitivity.note: same block count as E1, partition rebuilt per seed; fixed-parameter models (tuned once in E1), so this isolates partition uncertainty
same block count as E1, partition rebuilt per seed; fixed-parameter models (tuned once in E1), so this isolates partition uncertainty

interval.method: split-conformal, blocks held out for calibration, scored on unseen spatial test blocks
interval.honest_note: The nominal 90% interval is calibrated on held-out spatial blocks and scored on test blocks never seen; coverage below 0.90 means the interval is too narrow for new areas.

limitations: No low-cost sensor data: features are laboratory wet-chemistry values that a sensor could in principle proxy. Nothing here has been measured with the planned hardware.
No Ugandan field validation: predictions have not been checked against any soil sampled for this project.
Not validated for agronomic decisions: rates, timing, or certification claims must not be made from this prototype.
Laboratory values carry lab-to-lab bias; replicate records are collapsed, so measurement error is under-represented relative to a real sensor.
Prediction intervals are marginal (one width for all inputs), not conditional on the feature values.
